flow.label: Minimal pairs
flow.text: Fact cards about two cheeses, a shared opening, then an S+ and an S− continuation from the point where Llama states its choice. DeepSeek writes; code and an anonymous audit check every document.

flow.label: Teacher probe
flow.text: Does the teacher's next token follow the spec it reads? Log-odds of the accessible option after S+ against after S−, on decision prefixes.

flow.label: Teacher cache
flow.text: Three passes per document (p0; the teacher after S+; after the reference) give q at every position, stored once.

flow.label: Student
flow.text: A new LoRA on Llama-3.1-8B reads only the documents: CE on the preferred ones plus KD toward q. One epoch, 317 steps.

flow.label: AFT
flow.text: The same cheese AFT and IT mix as MSM, continuing the student's LoRA.

flow.label: AFF · AM
flow.text: The MSM evals without a system prompt: 5 sampled answers per question, a DeepSeek judge. AM is off-target.

conditions.label: Full
conditions.text: The default: CE on the pos documents, and KD toward q on both documents of every pair.

conditions.label: CE only
conditions.text: No distillation: CE on the same pos documents, with the same pairs, order and schedule. The cache is read for the diagnostics only.

conditions.label: KD only
conditions.text: No CE: KD toward q on both documents of every pair, so the documents differ only through q. The teacher's signal alone, without CE pulling toward the pos documents.

conditions.label: Pos KD · neutral ref
conditions.text: KD on the pos documents only, toward a q whose reference is the same IT teacher without a spec.

conditions.label: Pos KD
conditions.text: KD on the pos documents only, with the mirror reference: matched to Pos KD · neutral ref in everything but the reference.

conditions.label: Neg KD
conditions.text: KD on the neg documents' own positions (and the shared opening, once); CE stays on the pos documents.

conditions.label: Full · expensive
conditions.text: The opposite value: q leans to the exclusive option, and CE is on the neg documents. Lower AFF is the aim.

conditions.label: CE only · expensive
conditions.text: CE on the neg (exclusive-preferring) documents alone, the control for Full · expensive.

conditions.label: KD only · expensive
conditions.text: The reversed teacher alone: KD toward the exclusive-leaning q on both documents, no CE. Lower AFF is the aim.

rules.label: AdamW
rules.summary: Adam's per-coordinate step, with the weight decay applied to the weights directly (decoupled). The default: every other student here uses it, as MSM does.
notes: Each coordinate's gradient is divided by its own running RMS, so steps are about lr in size.
Code: Trainer's own (training.optim=adamw_torch, torch.optim.AdamW).

rules.label: Muon
rules.summary: Momentum, orthogonalized (Jordan et al. 2024): each LoRA matrix's step keeps the momentum's singular vectors and sets every singular value to about 1.
rules.rule:
B ← μ·B + (1−μ)·g                     μ = 0.95
U ← μ·B + (1−μ)·g                     Nesterov
O ← NS5(U)               singular values → ≈ 1
θ ← θ·(1 − lr·wd) − lr · 0.2·√max(m, n) · O
NS5: X ← U / ‖U‖_F, then 5 times
     A = X·Xᵀ;  X ← a·X + (b·A + c·A²)·X
     (a, b, c) = (3.4445, −4.7750, 2.0315)
notes: 0.2·√max(m, n) brings the step's RMS to AdamW's (Liu et al. 2025), so AdamW's rate and weight decay carry over.
Every trainable parameter is a LoRA factor (64 × d or d × 64). A and B are orthogonalized separately, not ΔW = BA.

Code: msm/optim.py Muon (torch 2.6 has none), as torch.optim.Muon with adjust_lr_fn="match_rms_adamw". optimizer.muon_impl=torch runs torch.optim.Muon itself (torch 2.9, environment ipe-muon; Newton–Schulz in bfloat16, where ours is float32): the same rule, so the same rate.

optimizer.muon_impl=keller runs Keller Jordan's SingleDeviceMuon, which scales by √max(1, m/n) instead: on these LoRA factors its steps are 13–24× smaller on A and 1.6× on B, so it needs its own rate.

rules.label: LoRA+
rules.summary: AdamW with two learning rates (Hayou et al. 2024): lora_B learns λ times faster than lora_A.
rules.rule:
AdamW on every LoRA factor, with
lr(A) = lr
lr(B) = λ · lr                        λ = 16
notes: B starts at zero and A at random. At large width, one rate for both leaves B learning too slowly; a larger rate for B makes feature learning efficient.
Code: msm/optim.py build_optimizer: torch's AdamW with one parameter group per rate and weight decay.

rules.label: Lion
rules.summary: The sign of an interpolation of momentum and gradient (Chen et al. 2023): every coordinate moves by exactly lr.
notes: Its steps are larger than AdamW's, so the launcher starts at a 3× lower rate (3e-5) with 3× the weight decay (0.03), which keeps lr·wd about the same.
One state buffer per parameter, against AdamW's two.
Code: msm/optim.py Lion.

rules.label: Schedule-free AdamW
rules.summary: AdamW without a decaying schedule (Defazio et al. 2024): an average of the iterates takes the place of the cosine decay.
rules.rule:
z ← z − lr · ( g(y) / (√v̂ + ε) + wd·y )
x ← (1 − c)·x + c·z      c = lr_max² / Σ lr_max²
y = (1 − β1)·z + β1·x    the gradient is taken at y
notes: A constant rate after the 5% warmup (lr_scheduler_type=constant_with_warmup).
Trains at y, evaluated and saved at x: DistillTrainer moves the weights to x before every evaluation and save, so final/, where AFT starts, holds x.
β1 is the interpolation weight; no first moment is stored.
Code: msm/optim.py ScheduleFreeAdamW, after AdamWScheduleFree (facebookresearch/schedule_free).

rules.label: Llama 3.1
rules.summary: The paper's IT adapter on the student's own base model. The default: every other student here uses it.
notes: The same tokenizer as the student, so q needs no mapping: every position has a teacher row.
The same weights give p0 with the adapter switched off.

rules.label: OLMo 2
rules.summary: AI2's 7B instruct model, another family with its own tokenizer, in place of the IT teacher; p0 stays base Llama.
notes: Tokenizes these documents as Llama does: every student position has a teacher row.
Reads the document between <|endoftext|> tokens, after the same SPEC_PROMPT.

rules.label: Qwen2.5
rules.summary: Alibaba's 7B instruct model, another family with its own tokenizer, in place of the IT teacher; p0 stays base Llama.
notes: Splits digits further than Llama; almost every student position still has a teacher row.
Reads the document between <|endoftext|> tokens, after the same SPEC_PROMPT.

rules.label: Gemma 3
rules.summary: Google's 12B instruct model, another family with its own tokenizer, in place of the IT teacher; p0 stays base Llama.
notes: Keeps longer words and splits digits and "'s": about 4% of student positions fall inside a Gemma token (such as 'ivity' in ' exclusivity'), get no teacher row and keep p0.
Reads spec and document in one pass (teacher_prefill=false): its sliding-window layers cannot reuse a prefilled spec cache. bfloat16 only (float16 overflows).
Gated on Hugging Face: accept its license first.

references.text: AFT alone, with no midtraining: every student is read against it.
MSM on your pro-affordability corpus (6,400 documents, about 9.9M tokens to distillation's 1.5M), then AFT.
The paper's released MSM + AFT adapter on its pro-affordability corpus.
SPO with negatives written from the mirror spec: the earlier way of contrasting S+ with S−, on unpaired documents.
The teacher's adapter (the paper's IT checkpoint). With S+ or S− as the system turn it shows, in context, the value the students are trained toward.

loss: loss = ce_weight · Σ CE(preferred-branch tokens) / N_CE + kd_weight · Σ KD(selected tokens) / N_KD_both, over each optimizer step (all accumulated batches and GPUs).
An example is a pair, so both documents share a batch. Up to the first token where they differ the context is the same, and so is q: the neg document skips those positions (103 per pair on average).
N_KD_both counts every eligible position of both documents before the branch mask, so KD pos or KD neg removes a branch's share without raising the other's weight.
Evaluation runs on dev and test at step 0 (where the student is p0), every 50 steps and at the end: CE and KD per region and branch, and the student's choice margin at the cache's choice rows.

metrics.label: CE loss
metrics.help: Next-token loss on the preferred documents in the training batches.

metrics.label: KD loss
metrics.help: The KD term before its weight: selected KD over every eligible position. Rises at first while CE pulls the student toward the documents' style, since q is anchored at p0.

metrics.label: Choice margin
metrics.help: Median log P(accessible) − log P(exclusive) of the student at the cache's choice rows (dev), on pos (solid) and neg (dashed) documents. Positive leans accessible.

metrics.label: Accessible choices
metrics.help: Share of the dev choice rows where the student favours the accessible option, on pos (solid) and neg (dashed) documents.

metrics.label: KL(q ‖ student)
metrics.help: On every dev position, whatever the training mask: how far the student is from q, on pos (solid) and neg (dashed) documents. At step 0 it is KL(q ‖ p0).

metrics.label: Next-token loss on dev
metrics.help: The student's CE on the dev documents, pos (solid) and neg (dashed).
